description:
Configure development and test profiles so failures retain useful line-number backtraces without embedding full debugger payloads in every test executable. Keep interactive incremental compilation explicit while ensuring broad gate builds do not accumulate incremental state.

## Background

A representative 246.7 MiB test executable contains 193.7 MiB of debug sections, and accumulated incremental state accounts for roughly 19 GiB. The repository currently has no manifest-level development or test profile policy.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The workspace manifest sets both development and test debug information to `line-tables-only`, and a representative failing test with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` reports a source file and line number from repository code.
- [hard] REQ-02: The workspace manifest explicitly enables the intended incremental behavior for ordinary interactive development and tests rather than relying on an undocumented Cargo default.
- [hard] REQ-03: `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` exports `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` for every Rust compilation step while preserving the manifest's interactive policy outside the gate.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every cargo-ci gate run deterministically verifies, as a failing gate step, that no non-empty Cargo incremental compilation state exists under the target directory that run actually used (an explicitly set CARGO_TARGET_DIR, else Cargo's resolved default), while still running formatting, zero-warning workspace all-target clippy, and the complete workspace test suite. Routine gate runs are not required to create isolated target directories; fresh isolated-CARGO_TARGET_DIR runs are the benchmark protocol's territory (dev/archive/6eb585bc-core-maintenance/dev/active/73482aa1-rust-build-efficiency.md) and must pass the same incremental-state step when exercised. [amended 2026-07-15, invoker-approved: codifies the plan's split between routine gate runs and isolated measurement samples]
- [hard] REQ-05: A regression test or deterministic policy assertion fails if either profile returns to full debug information or if the gate stops disabling incremental compilation.
title: Bound debug information and gate incremental state
